dedupe_keys.name: a global scale geodatabase of mine areas 24 605 polygons tang werner and co authors 2021

description: A global polygon dataset of mine areas, including open-cut pits, milling infrastructure, waste rock dumps and tailings storage facilities, with 24,605 polygons in total. The Zenodo record names Liang Tang and Shi Zeming of Chengdu University of Technology, Tim T. Werner of the University of Melbourne, Xie Heping of Shenzhen University and Yang Jingsong of the Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences among the creators. It was published on 12 July 2021 as a single downloadable RAR archive of shapefiles of about 21.7 MB, free under CC BY 4.0, and accompanies the article "A global-scale spatial assessment and geodatabase of mine areas" (Global and Planetary Change, 2021). Coverage is global. Caveats: attribute fields, imagery sources and dates are not described on the record read; the later global mining footprint from the same authors (74,548 polygons) supersedes it for most uses. For simulation it gives the extent of mine sites with their tailings and waste dumps, to check exposure of mines to floods, landslides and earthquakes and the infrastructure near them. Related catalogue records include the Tang and Werner global high-resolution mining footprints and the Maus global-scale mining polygons.
